page.title: Control bar
page.purpose: The hidden control layer. Absent until an input arrives, then reveals at remote-sized targets, acknowledges every command including the ones the browser refuses, and fades back out. It overlays every room rather than being a page of its own.

regions.purpose: Room navigation, cycle pause and resume, fullscreen, samples mode, and help. Every target at least 64px in kiosk mode.
The stated result of the last command: pending, succeeded, failed, or unavailable with a reason.
The intent map for every input class, so a person holding a remote can find out what the remote does.

states.description: Default. No input for four seconds; the control layer is not rendered and not focusable.
An input of any class arrived. Controls render at remote-sized targets with visible focus, and the cycle is paused.
A command the browser refuses — fullscreen or wake-lock on a TV browser. The acknowledgement region states that it is unavailable and why, in one line, without a dialog.
Controlled by a gamepad. Focus is visible at all times, D-pad moves between targets, and shoulder buttons change room without entering the bar.

priorities.statement: Hidden is the default, and hidden means absent.
priorities.notes: Not transparent, not collapsed — not rendered and not focusable. A control layer that is merely invisible still traps focus and still reads to a screen reader on an unattended display.

priorities.statement: Every command acknowledges, especially the ones that fail.
priorities.notes: Fullscreen and wake-lock fail silently on several TV browsers. Silence is indistinguishable from a broken remote, and someone will press the button repeatedly before concluding the board is broken.
DESIGN.md forbids blocking modal errors on an unattended display. A modal left open on a wall panel is a board that has stopped working with no one present to dismiss it.

priorities.statement: Every input class reaches every control.
priorities.notes: Nothing essential is behind hover. A gamepad, a keyboard, a touch screen and a mouse each reach every affordance here.

priorities.statement: The bar controls the view; it never controls the data.
priorities.notes: Samples mode changes what is displayed, not what is true. Nothing here writes anything anywhere.

claims.statement: In hidden state the control layer is neither rendered nor reachable by keyboard or gamepad focus.
claims.rationale: An invisible but focusable control layer produces a board where the first keypress goes somewhere the viewer cannot see.
claims.x-check-plan: While hidden, no control appears in the tab order.

claims.statement: Pointer movement, any keypress, a touch, and any gamepad action each reveal the control layer.
claims.rationale: A board reached from a phone, a desk and a remote cannot privilege one input class.
claims.x-check-plan: A gamepad, keyboard, touch and pointer event each move the surface from hidden to revealed.

claims.statement: A command the browser refuses produces a visible one-line statement naming the command and the reason, and no dialog.
claims.rationale: Silent failure on a remote is indistinguishable from a broken remote.
claims.x-check-plan: An unavailable command renders a stated reason rather than being silently inert.

claims.statement: Every interactive target is at least 64px in the kiosk presentation.
claims.rationale: DESIGN.md sets 64px for visible controls in TV and kiosk mode; a D-pad and a couch make smaller targets unusable.
claims.x-check-plan: Every interactive node in kiosk mode measures at least 64px on both axes.

claims.statement: Under gamepad or keyboard control the focused target is unambiguously visible at viewing distance.
claims.rationale: Spatial navigation with invisible focus is unusable, and this is the input class most likely to be tested last.
claims.x-check-plan: The focused control has a visible focus indicator meeting the contrast floor in every state.

claims.statement: No control writes a setpoint, files work, or mutates an upstream. Samples mode changes presentation only.
claims.rationale: The control bar is where a write path would feel most natural to add and would be least visible in review.
claims.x-check-plan: No interactive node declares a write intent and no mutating request is issued from this surface.
